title: [finding] `api.github.com` answered HTTP 200 from a dispatch container — the "unreachable from PR gates and dispatch containers" rationale two landed patrols rest on may no longer hold
body:
Measured while implementing #10803 (PR #11883) and deliberately not acted on there — the dev recorded it and handed the disposition to the PM seat, which is the right call, since it does not change that card's outcome but may weaken a rationale other cards lean on. Filing it unassigned for triage grading.

## The observation

`scripts/check-release-section-coverage.mjs` was compared against the two existing patrols, and #10803's card explains why **those two had to leave `lint.yml`**:

> Both of those had to move off `lint.yml` for a **transport** reason — they read `api.github.com`, which **PR gates and dispatch containers cannot reach**.

Measured during that dispatch: **`api.github.com` answered HTTP 200 from the dispatch container.**

## What that does and does not falsify

⚠️ Stated precisely, because the claim has two halves and only one was tested:

| half of the claim | status |
|:---|:---|
| "**dispatch containers** cannot reach `api.github.com`" | **falsified** for this container, today, by a 200 |
| "**PR gates** cannot reach `api.github.com`" | ⛔ **not tested.** No reading was taken from inside a PR-gate job |

So this is not "the rationale is wrong". It is "half of the rationale is measurably not true in one of the two environments it names, and nobody has re-checked the other half."

⚠️ Also unmeasured: whether the 200 reflects an *authenticated, useful* reachability or merely that the host answers. A patrol needs the former.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a footnote

Two landed workflows justify both their **existence** and their **placement** on this claim:

- `half-state-patrol.yml` — *"A healing mechanism with no scheduled caller heals only in the counterfactual."*
- `required-set-patrol.yml` — *"It shipped with no standing caller, so the only thing CI ran was its OFFLINE self-test."*

Neither of those two statements depends on reachability — they are about callers, and they stand. What depends on reachability is the **separate** decision that each had to become its own scheduled workflow rather than a step in `lint.yml`. If that constraint has lapsed, then:

1. the stated reason on two landed workflows is stale prose — the **"a prohibition rots because the thing it describes was widened while the prose stating it was not"** class this repo has now paid for at least three times (#10163, #10854, and the `findUp` prose repair in flight today);
2. more expensively, **the next card that needs a scheduled workflow inherits a false constraint** and routes around a problem that may not exist. #10803 itself came within one measurement of doing exactly that — its answer happened not to depend on reachability (the reason there is *audience*, not transport), so the stale claim cost nothing that time.

## Not claimed

- ⛔ **No proposal.** Whether the answer is re-measuring both environments, narrowing the prose to what is still true, or leaving it alone because the patrols are correctly placed for other reasons, is a triage judgment.
- ⛔ **Nothing is broken today.** Both patrols work. This is about the accuracy of a reason, not the correctness of a mechanism — which is precisely the class that goes unnoticed until someone re-derives a decision from it.
- The reading is **one container, one moment**. A second reading from a PR-gate job is the measurement that would settle it, and it has not been taken.

## Refs

#10803 / PR #11883 (where it was measured) · #9844 and #9678 (the two patrols' own cards) · #10854 and #10163 (the same rotting-prose class, different content)
